library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)

# Model and source

```{r meta, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
mod <- readModelDb("vanderGaag_2026_piflufolastat_pbpk")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
cat("* Citation: ", ui$reference, "\n", sep = "")
cat("* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1111/cts.70583>\n")
cat("* Authors' model code: <https://github.com/ibartelink/Target-Site-PBPK-in-oncology>\n")
cat("* ODE states: ", length(ui$state), " (74 from the paper plus two cumulative-elimination states)\n", sep = "")
```

van der Gaag and co-workers rebuilt the Begum 2018 whole-body PBPK model of
PSMA-targeting radioligands and adapted it to the diagnostic PET tracer
[18F]F-piflufolastat ([18F]DCFPyL). The model has eleven PSMA-expressing tissues
with receptor binding, internalisation and release of internalised ligand; a
kidney in which the tracer is filtered into the tubular lumen, binds PSMA there,
and is excreted in urine; and eight PSMA-negative tissues with vascular and
interstitial spaces. All parameters are fixed physiological or literature
values. Only the tumour PSMA receptor density was fitted, per patient, to the
120 min PET image. The authors then used each patient's fitted density to
predict the therapeutic ligand [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617.

The packaged model doses the injected amount in nmol (activity divided by the
specific activity, 0.045 GBq/nmol) into `venous`. It returns the arterial serum
concentration `Cc` (nmol/L) and decay-corrected tissue activity concentrations
`act_<tissue>` (kBq/mL), the unit of the paper's Table S3.

# Population

Table 2 of the paper lists 15 men with metastatic prostate cancer from Amsterdam
UMC. The **internal** cohort is 8 patients with dynamic PET from 0 to 120 min.
The **external** cohort is 5 patients with a single total-body PET/CT at
120 min. The **therapeutic** cohort is 2 patients who also had 24 h and 7 day
SPECT after their first cycle of [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617. Ages were 56-86 years,
weights 64-119 kg and heights 170-191 cm; the tracer dose was 245-319 MBq. Per
patient haematocrit and eGFR were not published. This vignette uses the Table S4
prostate-cancer population means (43.3 % and 83 mL/min) for every patient.

```{r cohort}
tab2 <- data.frame(
  id = 1:15,
  cohort = rep(c("internal", "external", "therapeutic"), c(8, 5, 2)),
  AGE = c(67, 63, 68, 65, 71, 81, 71, 56, 78, 82, 75, 86, 73, 72, 75),
  HT = c(171, 191, 187, 181, 177, 173, 181, 186, 178, 184, 181, 184, 179, 182, 170),
  WT = c(100, 119, 80, 81, 64, 98, 85, 104, 72, 90, 108, 77, 81, 82, 90),
  MBq = c(319.4, 301.9, 303.8, 283.8, 303.6, 245.3, 292.8, 317.1,
          313.5, 317.0, 308.4, 314.5, 319.1, 279.4, 285.3),
  vol_tu1 = c(5.18, 6.66, 6.85, 14.40, 27.58, 6.27, 5.31, 5.82,
              38.29, 36.55, 63.12, 35.83, 4.36, 1.98, 8.16),
  vol_tu2 = c(3.58, 6.53, 2.62, 9.86, 21.38, 6.21, 4.54, 3.01, rep(NA, 5), 1.69, NA),
  vol_rest = c(10.82, 19.20, 1.73, 14.46, 69.31, 26.24, 11.58, 3.07, rep(NA, 5), 1.82, NA),
  # Table S2: tumour receptor density fitted to the 120 min PET (nmol/L)
  rd_fit = c(177.954, 8.63152, 2.45811, 5.32467, 13.4815, 34.1339, 197.896, 31.7173,
             1.11941, 7.6961, 13.4814, 2.394, 24.2184, 29.7169, 69.7354)
)
# External patients have only a total tumour volume, and patient 15 a single
# lesion: that volume goes into lesion 1 and the other two lesions get a
# negligible volume (the model needs strictly positive volumes).
tiny <- 1e-6
tab2 <- tab2 |>
  mutate(
    ORGVOL_TUMOR1 = vol_tu1,
    ORGVOL_TUMOR2 = ifelse(is.na(vol_tu2), tiny, vol_tu2),
    ORGVOL_TUMORREST = ifelse(is.na(vol_rest), tiny, vol_rest),
    HCT = 43.3,
    CRCL = 83,
    dose_nmol = MBq / 1000 / 0.045
  )
knitr::kable(
  tab2 |>
    select(id, cohort, AGE, HT, WT, MBq, vol_tu1, vol_tu2, vol_rest, rd_fit) |>
    rename(
      "Patient" = id, "Cohort" = cohort, "Age (y)" = AGE, "Height (cm)" = HT,
      "Weight (kg)" = WT, "Dose (MBq)" = MBq, "Tumour 1 (mL)" = vol_tu1,
      "Tumour 2 (mL)" = vol_tu2, "Tumour rest (mL)" = vol_rest,
      "Fitted receptor density (nmol/L)" = rd_fit
    ),
  caption = "Table 2 and Table S2 of van der Gaag 2026. For patients 9-13 the tumour 1 column holds the total tumour volume."
)
```

# Source trace

| Model element | Value / form | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Venous and arterial balance | Suppl. Eq 1-2 | Supporting Information Part A |
| Kidney vascular, lumen, bound, internalised, free receptor | Suppl. Eq 3, 10, 12, 13, 15 | Part A |
| Lung, liver (arterial + splenic + GI inflow), brain (vascular only), other tissues | Suppl. Eq 4-7, 9 | Part A |
| PSMA-tissue interstitial, bound, internalised, free receptor | Suppl. Eq 8, 11, 13, 14 | Part A |
| `kon` 0.046 L/nmol/min, `kd` 0.49 nmol/L | piflufolastat column | Table 1 |
| `phi_kid` 0.75 (sieving), `fraex` 0.96 (excreted fraction) | piflufolastat column | Table 1 |
| `aspec` 0.045 GBq/nmol | piflufolastat column | Table 1 |
| `kint` 0.001; `krel_tumor` 1.4e-4; `krel_kidney` 2.3e-4; `krel_parotid` 3.7e-4 1/min | Labda int / Labda rel | Table S1, section 1a |
| `fdens_tumor1` 0.1351538, `fdens_tumor2` 0.2676154 mL/min/g; `xf_tumorrest` 0.53 | F dens,tu1/2, X F | Table S1; Results "fixed at 0.135" |
| `rdens_tumor1` 44.93846, `rdens_tumor2` 47.38462 nmol/L; `xr_tumorrest` 1.4 | R dens,tu1/2, X R | Table S1 |
| `rdens_kidney` 18, `rdens_parotid` 42 nmol/L; prostate, liver, spleen, GI derived | R dens rows | Table S1 |
| BSA (Du Bois), serum volume 2.8(1-H)BSA, total flow 1.23 V_ser | formulas | Table S1 |
| Organ total, vascular and interstitial volumes; alpha ratios | formulas | Table S1 |
| Organ flows (fractions of F_tot, flow densities, F_k,age = 4.3 - 0.026 Age) | formulas | Table S1 |
| PS products (K_i x V_tot,i) | K rows | Table S1 |
| F_fil = eGFR x sieving, F_ex = F_fil x Fra_ex | formulas | Table S1 with Table 1 values |
| Covariates: age, height, weight, tumour volumes | per patient | Table 2 |
| Fitted tumour receptor density per patient | per patient | Table S2 |
| Haematocrit 43.3 %, eGFR 83 mL/min (population means) | used for every patient | Table S4 |

# Mass balance

The model conserves ligand exactly: the free, bound and internalised amounts,
plus the cumulative urinary excretion and the cumulative release of internalised
ligand, always sum to the injected dose. The free-receptor states are excluded
from the sum because they count receptors, not ligand.

```{r mass-balance}
ligand_states <- setdiff(ui$state, grep("^rfree_", ui$state, value = TRUE))
p1 <- tab2[1, ]
ev_mb <- rbind(
  data.frame(id = 1, time = 0, amt = p1$dose_nmol, evid = 1, cmt = "venous"),
  data.frame(id = 1, time = c(1, 10, 60, 120, 1440, 10080), amt = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "venous")
) |>
  cbind(p1[, c("AGE", "HT", "WT", "HCT", "CRCL", "ORGVOL_TUMOR1", "ORGVOL_TUMOR2", "ORGVOL_TUMORREST")])
sim_mb <- as.data.frame(rxSolve(mod, ev_mb, atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-8))
sim_mb$total <- rowSums(sim_mb[, ligand_states])
knitr::kable(
  sim_mb |>
    mutate(rel_err = (total - p1$dose_nmol) / p1$dose_nmol) |>
    select(time, total, urine, released, rel_err) |>
    rename("Time (min)" = time, "Total ligand (nmol)" = total,
           "Cumulative urine (nmol)" = urine, "Cumulative released (nmol)" = released,
           "Relative error vs dose" = rel_err),
  digits = 6
)
stopifnot(max(abs(sim_mb$total - p1$dose_nmol)) / p1$dose_nmol < 1e-5)
```

# Internal cohort: 0-120 min profiles

Figure 2 of the paper shows the tumour, arterial blood, lung and muscle
time-activity curves of the eight internal patients. The packaged model is
simulated twice for each patient: with the typical Table S1 tumour receptor
densities (the model defaults) and with that patient's fitted density from
Table S2. The fitted density is applied to both delineated lesions. The rest
tumour follows Table S1 (1.4 times the mean lesion density). The open points
are the paper's observed values at 120 min (Table S3).

```{r internal-sim}
covcols <- c("AGE", "HT", "WT", "HCT", "CRCL", "ORGVOL_TUMOR1", "ORGVOL_TUMOR2", "ORGVOL_TUMORREST")
make_events <- function(pts, times) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(pts)), function(i) {
    p <- pts[i, ]
    rbind(
      data.frame(id = p$id, time = 0, amt = p$dose_nmol, evid = 1, cmt = "venous"),
      data.frame(id = p$id, time = times, amt = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "venous")
    ) |>
      cbind(p[rep(1, length(times) + 1), c(covcols, "rd_fit")], row.names = NULL)
  }))
}
internal <- tab2 |> filter(cohort == "internal")
times_int <- c(seq(0.5, 10, by = 0.5), seq(11, 120, by = 1))
ev_int <- make_events(internal, times_int)

sim_typ <- as.data.frame(rxSolve(mod, ev_int, atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-8)) |>
  mutate(density = "Table S1 typical")
ev_fit <- ev_int |> mutate(rdens_tumor1 = rd_fit, rdens_tumor2 = rd_fit)
sim_fit <- as.data.frame(rxSolve(mod, ev_fit, atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-8)) |>
  mutate(density = "Table S2 fitted")
sim_int <- bind_rows(sim_typ, sim_fit)
```

```{r fig2, fig.height = 8, fig.cap = "Replicates the layout of Figure 2 of van der Gaag 2026 (internal patients 1-8). Lines: packaged model; points: observed activity at 120 min (Table S3)."}
tab_s3_int <- data.frame(
  id = 1:8,
  tumor1 = c(130, 41.7, 12.8, 23.2, 61.1, 65.3, 93.3, 81.4),
  blood = c(3.70, 2.83, 4.42, 5.26, 1.79, 2.72, 3.01, 3.65),
  lungs = c(2.69, 1.52, 2.02, 1.36, 2.83, 1.04, 1.48, 1.61),
  muscle = c(2.94, 1.63, 2.17, 2.10, 2.01, 1.22, 0.78, 1.28)
)
pred_s3_int <- data.frame(
  id = 1:8,
  tumor1 = c(125, 33.1, 12.4, 22.4, 59.3, 62.9, 90.4, 78.7),
  blood = c(14.0, 10.5, 11.7, 12.2, 14.0, 9.47, 10.8, 11.5),
  lungs = c(7.99, 5.81, 7.26, 7.85, 9.09, 5.95, 7.05, 6.53),
  muscle = c(1.18, 0.84, 1.19, 1.31, 1.55, 0.97, 1.20, 0.97)
)
long_sim <- sim_int |>
  select(id, time, density, tumor1 = act_tumor1, blood = act_blood,
         lungs = act_lungs, muscle = act_muscle) |>
  pivot_longer(c(tumor1, blood, lungs, muscle), names_to = "tissue", values_to = "kBq_mL")
long_obs <- tab_s3_int |>
  pivot_longer(-id, names_to = "tissue", values_to = "kBq_mL") |>
  mutate(time = 120)
ggplot(long_sim, aes(time, kBq_mL, colour = tissue)) +
  geom_line(aes(linetype = density)) +
  geom_point(data = long_obs, shape = 1, size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~id, ncol = 2, labeller = label_both) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after injection (min)", y = "Activity concentration (kBq/mL)",
       colour = "Tissue", linetype = "Tumour receptor density") +
  theme_bw()
```

## Comparison with the paper's 120 min predictions (Table S3)

```{r s3-internal}
at120 <- sim_fit |>
  filter(time == 120) |>
  select(id, tumor1 = act_tumor1, blood = act_blood, lungs = act_lungs, muscle = act_muscle) |>
  pivot_longer(-id, names_to = "tissue", values_to = "sim")
cmp_int <- pred_s3_int |>
  pivot_longer(-id, names_to = "tissue", values_to = "paper_pred") |>
  left_join(at120, by = c("id", "tissue")) |>
  left_join(long_obs |> select(id, tissue, obs = kBq_mL), by = c("id", "tissue")) |>
  mutate(ratio = sim / paper_pred)
cmp_int |>
  group_by(tissue) |>
  summarise(
    median_ratio = median(ratio), min_ratio = min(ratio), max_ratio = max(ratio),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  rename("Tissue" = tissue, "Median sim / paper pred" = median_ratio,
         "Min" = min_ratio, "Max" = max_ratio) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Packaged model (Table S2 fitted tumour density) against the paper's predicted 120 min values, internal patients 1-8.")
knitr::kable(
  cmp_int |> filter(tissue == "tumor1") |>
    select(id, obs, paper_pred, sim, ratio) |>
    rename("Patient" = id, "Observed" = obs, "Paper predicted" = paper_pred,
           "Packaged model" = sim, "Model / paper" = ratio),
  digits = 2,
  caption = "Tumour lesion 1 at 120 min (kBq/mL), Table S3 against the packaged model with the Table S2 fitted density."
)
blood_ratio <- cmp_int$ratio[cmp_int$tissue == "blood"]
muscle_ratio <- cmp_int$ratio[cmp_int$tissue == "muscle"]
# Blood and muscle depend only on the systemic physiology, so a mis-transcribed
# flow, volume or excretion term would shift every patient together.
stopifnot(
  abs(median(blood_ratio) - 1) < 0.25,
  abs(median(muscle_ratio) - 1) < 0.35
)
```

Blood and muscle reproduce the paper's predicted values within about 20 %.
The remaining scatter is expected: the paper used each patient's own haematocrit
and eGFR, which were not published, and this vignette uses population means.

Two tissues do **not** reproduce, and the vignette shows that openly:

* **Lungs** come out at about half the paper's predicted values. The packaged
  lung vascular volume is Table S1's `V_tot,lu x 0.055`. The authors' code uses
  `0.105 x V_ser,body` instead, which is about four times larger. The section
  below shows that the code's lung volume closes most of the gap.
* **Tumour lesion 1** with the Table S2 fitted density comes out 1.5-4 times the
  paper's predicted value. The mapping from the single fitted density in
  Table S2 to the three tumour compartments is not described. The fitting
  script is not in the authors' repository either. The model's own tumour
  dynamics can be checked, but the published per-patient tumour predictions
  cannot be regenerated from what was published.

## Sensitivity: lung vascular volume

```{r lung-sensitivity}
mod_codelung <- mod |> model(vv_lungs <- 0.105 * vser)
sim_cl <- as.data.frame(rxSolve(mod_codelung, ev_fit |> filter(time %in% c(0, 120)), atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-8)) |>
  filter(time == 120)
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    id = 1:8,
    paper_pred = pred_s3_int$lungs,
    table_s1 = sim_fit$act_lungs[sim_fit$time == 120],
    code_volume = sim_cl$act_lungs
  ) |>
    rename("Patient" = id, "Paper predicted" = paper_pred,
           "Packaged (Table S1 lung volume)" = table_s1,
           "With the code's lung volume" = code_volume),
  digits = 2,
  caption = "Lung activity at 120 min (kBq/mL)."
)
```

# External cohort (120 min, Table S3)

The five external patients have only a total tumour volume, so it is placed in
lesion 1. The fitted density from Table S2 is used for both lesions.

```{r external}
external <- tab2 |> filter(cohort == "external")
ev_ext <- make_events(external, 120) |> mutate(rdens_tumor1 = rd_fit, rdens_tumor2 = rd_fit)
sim_ext <- as.data.frame(rxSolve(mod, ev_ext, atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-8)) |> filter(time == 120)
pred_s3_ext <- data.frame(
  id = 9:13,
  tumor1 = c(30.6, 123, 197, 46.7, 247),
  lungs = c(12.1, 7.90, 7.05, 12.9, 8.19),
  muscle = c(2.20, 1.23, 1.03, 2.07, 1.31),
  kidney = c(52.3, 194, 160, 1.14, 215),
  spleen = c(82.2, 73.7, 70.6, 92.9, 75.0),
  liver = c(9.55, 8.12, 7.74, 11.3, 8.26),
  parotid = c(237, 219, 201, 286, 230)
)
obs_s3_ext <- data.frame(
  id = 9:13,
  tumor1 = c(31.7, 138, 203, 48.5, 254),
  lungs = c(1.97, 1.48, 1.42, 1.72, 1.58),
  muscle = c(2.68, 1.27, 1.05, 1.59, 1.30),
  kidney = c(48.7, 80.7, 164, 128, 73.6),
  spleen = c(30.7, 7.33, 5.75, 9.68, 13.3),
  liver = c(31.6, 20.3, 24.8, 25.7, 21.7),
  parotid = c(83.5, 47.4, 35.3, 76.4, 97.2)
)
sim_ext_long <- sim_ext |>
  select(id, tumor1 = act_tumor1, lungs = act_lungs, muscle = act_muscle,
         kidney = act_kidney, spleen = act_spleen, liver = act_liver, parotid = act_parotid) |>
  pivot_longer(-id, names_to = "tissue", values_to = "sim")
cmp_ext <- pred_s3_ext |>
  pivot_longer(-id, names_to = "tissue", values_to = "paper_pred") |>
  left_join(obs_s3_ext |> pivot_longer(-id, names_to = "tissue", values_to = "obs"), by = c("id", "tissue")) |>
  left_join(sim_ext_long, by = c("id", "tissue"))
cmp_ext |>
  group_by(tissue) |>
  summarise(obs = median(obs), paper_pred = median(paper_pred), sim = median(sim), .groups = "drop") |>
  rename("Tissue" = tissue, "Observed (median)" = obs,
         "Paper predicted (median)" = paper_pred, "Packaged model (median)" = sim) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "External patients 9-13 at 120 min (kBq/mL).")
```

For tumour, muscle, spleen and parotid, the medians of the packaged model are
close to the medians of the paper's predictions. Lung is about half, as in the
internal cohort. Liver is lower and kidney higher than the paper's
predictions. The paper's own predictions for spleen, liver, lung and parotid
already miss the observed values by about two-fold or more (Table S3). The
paper's Discussion attributes this to translating the Begum framework across
ligands, and the packaged model shares that limitation. For patient 12, Table S3
prints a predicted kidney value of 1.14 kBq/mL against an observed 128. That
predicted value is almost certainly a typo.

# Extrapolation to [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617

The paper swaps in the [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 column of Table 1 (`kon` 0.1
L/nmol/min, `kd` 3.3 nmol/L, sieving 0.66, excreted fraction 0.67). It keeps
each patient's fitted tumour density from the diagnostic scan and simulates a
7.4 GBq therapeutic dose. Table 1 lists the specific activity of
[177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 as "not determined". The authors' code uses 82000 kBq/nmol
(0.082 GBq/nmol), and that value is used here to convert activity to nmol. The
SPECT data were decay-corrected to injection time, so the model carries no
physical decay.

```{r lu177}
mod_lu <- mod |> ini(kon = 0.1, kd = 3.3, phi_kid = 0.66, fraex = 0.67, aspec = 0.082)
thera <- tab2 |> filter(cohort == "therapeutic") |> mutate(dose_nmol = 7.4 / 0.082)
ev_lu <- make_events(thera, c(1440, 10080)) |> mutate(rdens_tumor1 = rd_fit, rdens_tumor2 = rd_fit)
sim_lu <- as.data.frame(rxSolve(mod_lu, ev_lu, atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-8)) |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  select(id, time, tumor1 = act_tumor1, kidney = act_kidney, parotid = act_parotid) |>
  pivot_longer(c(tumor1, kidney, parotid), names_to = "tissue", values_to = "sim")
ref_lu <- data.frame(
  id = rep(c(14, 15), each = 6),
  time = rep(rep(c(1440, 10080), each = 3), 2),
  tissue = rep(c("tumor1", "kidney", "parotid"), 4),
  obs = c(2670, 306, 3054, 1346, 53.0, 160, 2058, 595, 10343, 620, NA, 750),
  paper_pred = c(4966, 478, 2242, 1346, 62.1, 83.3, 2332, 484, 2281, 630, NA, 85.0)
)
knitr::kable(
  ref_lu |>
    left_join(sim_lu, by = c("id", "time", "tissue")) |>
    mutate(time = ifelse(time == 1440, "24 h", "7 d")) |>
    rename("Patient" = id, "Time" = time, "Tissue" = tissue, "Observed" = obs,
           "Paper predicted" = paper_pred, "Packaged model" = sim),
  digits = 1,
  caption = "[177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 activity (kBq/mL) after 7.4 GBq, Table S3 therapeutic rows."
)
```

Patient 15 has one delineated lesion, and its tumour matches the paper's
prediction within 3 % at both times. Kidney is within about 10 % of the paper's
prediction for both patients. Patient 14 has three small lesions, and its
tumour comes out about five times lower than the paper's prediction. This is
the same unpublished mapping from fitted density to compartments that affects
the internal cohort. Parotid is about half the paper's prediction, and both the
model and the paper's prediction under-predict the observed salivary uptake.

# Non-compartmental summary (PKNCA)

The paper reports no NCA. To give a reproducible exposure summary of the
diagnostic tracer, PKNCA is run on the arterial serum and tumour lesion 1
activity curves from the internal-cohort simulation with the Table S2 fitted
densities, over the 0-120 min imaging window.

```{r pknca}
nca_in <- sim_fit |>
  select(id, time, blood = act_blood, tumor1 = act_tumor1) |>
  pivot_longer(c(blood, tumor1), names_to = "tissue", values_to = "conc") |>
  bind_rows(expand.grid(id = 1:8, time = 0, tissue = c("blood", "tumor1"), conc = 0,
                        stringsAsFactors = FALSE)) |>
  distinct(id, tissue, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(tissue, id, time) |>
  filter(!is.na(conc))
dose_in <- internal |> transmute(id, time = 0, dose = MBq)
conc_obj <- PKNCAconc(nca_in, conc ~ time | tissue + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCAdose(dose_in, dose ~ time | id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 120, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca_res <- pk.nca(PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
summary(nca_res)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Source precedence.** The authors' public code (repository
  `ibartelink/Target-Site-PBPK-in-oncology`, PSMA files dated 2025-06-06)
  disagrees with the paper on several constants. In the code, `kon` is 0.09,
  sieving 0.66 and tumour flow density 0.26 mL/min/g; the organ volumes and
  receptor densities differ; and all filtrate returns to the blood, so nothing
  is excreted. The paper's Results ("flow density was fixed at 0.135") and its
  Table 1 contradict the code, which appears to be an earlier version. The
  maintainers therefore followed the paper: Table 1 (piflufolastat column),
  Table S1 and Suppl. Eq 1-15. The code was used only where the paper is
  internally inconsistent, as listed below.
* **Sieving and excreted fraction.** Table 1 gives the tracer-specific sieving
  0.75 and excreted fraction 0.96. Table S1 prints the generic values
  `Phi kid = 1` and `Fra ex = 1`. The Table 1 values are used.
* **Renal lumen mass balance.** Suppl. Eq 3 returns `F_ret` from the lumen to the
  kidney vasculature, but Suppl. Eq 10 drains only `F_ex` from the lumen. With
  `Fra_ex` = 0.96, `F_ret` = 0.04 `F_fil` is non-zero. The lumen therefore drains
  `F_ex + F_ret`, which conserves mass and matches the code. Excreted ligand is
  accumulated in the `urine` state.
* **Prostate volume.** Table S1 prints `(0.016+BW)/71`, which gives a prostate
  of about 1.1 L. The intended `0.016 x BW / 71` (the ICRP-23 form, as in the
  code) is used.
* **Rest-tumour flow.** Table S1 defines `F_dens,turest = X_F x mean(F_dens,tu1,
  F_dens,tu2)` but then prints `F_turest = F_dens,pro x V_tot,turest`, which
  leaves `F_dens,turest` unused. The defined rest-tumour flow density is used,
  as in the code. The two give similar values (about 0.107 against 0.102
  mL/min/g at H = 0.433).
* **Duplicated `K_pro`.** Table S1 lists the prostate permeability density twice
  (0.1 and 0.02 mL/min/g). The code's 0.1 is used.
* **`K_rest`.** It is not tabulated, although `PS_rest = K_rest x V_tot,rest` is.
  The code's 0.02 mL/min/g, the muscle-like value, is used.
* **Brain.** Suppl. Eq 6 is vascular only, with no interstitial state.
* **GI volume.** Table S1's coefficient sum `(0.395 + 0.548 + 0.104 + 0.15)` is
  used. The code and Begum 2018 use 0.385 for the first term, which makes the
  GI volume 0.8 % smaller.
* **Sums for the rest compartment.** `V_tot,rest`, `V_vasc,rest` and `F_rest` are
  "total minus the sum of all tissues" (Table S1). The sums include the venous
  and arterial pools and all three tumour compartments, as in the code.
* **`X_V`.** Table S1 lists a measured-to-actual rest-tumour volume ratio of
  0.64, but no equation uses it, and neither does the code. The measured
  rest-tumour volume is used directly.
* **Receptor densities.** The model defaults are the typical Table S1 values. The
  Table S2 per-patient fits are applied by overriding `rdens_tumor1` and
  `rdens_tumor2`. Following Table S1, the rest-tumour, prostate, liver and GI
  densities are derived from the lesion densities and change with them.
* **Haematocrit and eGFR.** These were not published per patient. The Table S4
  population means (43.3 %, 83 mL/min) are used for everyone, which explains
  part of the blood and muscle scatter against Table S3.
* **Blood output.** `act_blood` is the arterial serum concentration, as in the
  model's arterial balance. The paper does not state whether its image-derived
  blood value is whole blood or serum.
* **[177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 specific activity.** Table 1 gives "not determined". The
  code's 0.082 GBq/nmol is used in the extrapolation section. Activity
  concentrations scale with the injected activity, so this value matters only
  through receptor saturation.
* **Tumour and lung non-reproduction.** See the internal-cohort section. These
  are reported, not tuned.
* **Not reproduced.** The precision-dosing distribution (Figure 4B) needs
  per-patient haematocrit and eGFR, which were not published.
